analysis.title: China: The ingredients for a squeeze
key_insights: China has added $5 trillion to GDP since Covid, yet its equities have underperformed global markets by 110 percentage points.
Goldman sees 10% trend EPS growth and potential valuation upside of 10-15% for China equities.
The report attributes the gap between growth and shareholder returns to subsidies, overcapacity and competition that pushed companies to chase volume over profitability.
Goldman forecasts normalized ROE of 12% over the next five years. AI adoption, global expansion and anti-involution policies could drive a 10-15% valuation re-rating.
Nvidia's share of Chinese data-center AI accelerator shipments fell to 34% in H1 2026, with Huawei at 28%. TS Lombard argues US export restrictions are accelerating domestic chip substitution.
TS Lombard says China added roughly ten times as much generating capacity as the US in 2025, and electricity costs at some Chinese data-center hubs are around half the US industrial average.
Hartnett reports a record $86 billion of national-team inflows into China over the past four weeks.
ChiNext is approaching its 21-day moving average. A close above it would open the door to a squeeze, and a rebound toward the 50-day MA would be a substantial move.
STAR 50 remains below its downward-sloping trendline but has reclaimed its 21-day MA. A few percent higher would put the trendline under pressure.
The Market Ear concludes that China remains technically damaged, a new bull market is not confirmed, and the risk of being aggressively short China is rising.
